countries.name: Yemen
notes: First Middle East market. Five-year licence granted by the internationally recognised government in September 2024; commercial sales scaled up during 2025.
Service scope shaped by the civil war and the 2026 Bab al-Mandab crisis; coverage in Houthi-held areas is not sanctioned.

countries.name: Qatar
notes: Individual licence for public satellite networks issued September 2022; local entity Starlink Satellite Qatar W.L.L.
Qatar Airways signed the first Gulf in-flight Wi-Fi deal in May 2024 and rolled Starlink across its 777 fleet.
Consumer offer remains business-oriented rather than mass residential.

countries.name: Israel
notes: Approved in early 2024 with the service initially limited in scope. Listed as "Available now" on Starlink's map.

countries.name: Oman
notes: First GCC state with both residential and business plans, announced 27 March 2025 after TRA approval.
Framed by regulators as redundancy for fibre and coverage for remote/offshore energy sites.

countries.name: Jordan
notes: TRC ran the region's first live tests in late 2022 (100–200 Mbps in the south) but consumer launch waited until April 2025.
Positioned for remote communities lacking fixed broadband.

countries.name: Bahrain
notes: TRA licensed a SpaceX subsidiary as early as April 2022, one of the earliest approvals worldwide; service only became available in mid-May 2025, a 37-month gap.

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.price: Kit KWD 209 (Standard) / KWD 179 (Mini); data plans 500 GB–5 TB
notes: Musk announced availability on 14 March 2026, two weeks into the Iran war and after licensing delays flagged in January.
Distributed through Sama X (Alghanim Industries) as authorised reseller, with monthly no-contract plans.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.price: AED 230/mo Residential Lite; ~AED 300/mo Residential; kit AED 1,545
notes: TDRA issued a 10-year maritime-only licence in 2024; in-flight service on Emirates and flydubai followed in 2025.
Consumer service appeared on the availability map 18 March 2026.
A full 10-year General Space Services Licence was granted 28 August 2026 and formally announced 3 September, covering individuals, businesses and government.

countries.name: Iraq
notes: Cabinet approved the licence 17 June 2026; CMC signed it in Washington on 17 July during the prime minister's US visit.
Subscriptions opened on Starlink's site in late July. On 27 September the CMC reiterated the service is legal and that authorities can identify every terminal and owner.

Open dispute: the Communications Minister claimed in August that the serving gateway is in Qatar and pushed FTTH as the national priority; the CMC denies the data-sovereignty claim but concedes there is no in-country gateway yet.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
notes: Approval for aviation and maritime announced by Musk at the Saudi-US Investment Forum, 13 May 2025.
A local entity, Starlink KSA, is registered; CST has not published a residential or business licence. Starlink's map shows "Pending regulatory approval".

countries.name: Lebanon
notes: Licence granted, but connectivity has not been activated (as of March 2026 reporting). Earlier pilot deployments predate the licence.
The war that began 2 March 2026 and the ceasefire since 16 April leave the launch timetable uncertain.

countries.name: Egypt
notes: Sits in Starlink's "service date unknown" bucket; no licence application outcome has been made public.

countries.name: Iran
notes: Use of Starlink is illegal domestically. SpaceX switched beams on around 9 January 2026 during the protest-era internet blackout; access via smuggled terminals was reportedly free for a period.
Authorities seized hundreds of terminals in March 2026 after US–Israeli strikes; state media declared Starlink a "legitimate target" on 1 April 2026.

countries.name: Syria
notes: Explicitly listed as banned in Starlink's own availability data (May 2026), alongside Russia, China and Afghanistan.
